workflow: Manual role assignment when a member joins a specific voice channel (e.g., for a game lobby or support queue).
trigger: Member joins a designated voice channel.
frequency: Per-event (each time a member joins the voice channel)
current_workaround: Use third-party bots like YAGPDB or MEE6 with custom commands, or manually assign roles via the member list.
consequence: If not done, members miss channel-specific permissions or community alerts; manual assignment is slow and error-prone for large servers.

workflow: Manual review and removal of spam messages that bypass Discord's built-in AutoMod (e.g., repeated links, scam messages using character manipulation).
trigger: Spam message posted in a channel.
current_workaround: Use third-party moderation bots with custom regex filters (e.g., Dyno, Carl-bot) or manually delete messages and ban users.
consequence: Spam reaches members, damaging community trust; manual cleanup takes moderator time and can miss subtle spam patterns.

workflow: Manual tracking of role permissions and hierarchy using spreadsheets to avoid permission conflicts in large multi-community servers.
trigger: Adding a new role or modifying permissions for existing roles.
current_workaround: Maintain a separate spreadsheet mapping roles → permissions → channel overrides, or use a third-party bot that logs permission changes.
consequence: Permission errors can lead to security breaches or accidental data exposure; manual spreadsheet updates are error-prone and not real-time.

workflow: Manual backup of server configuration (roles, channels, permissions) and message history by exporting data via third-party tools or bots.
trigger: Server restructuring, fear of accidental deletion, or migration to a new server.
current_workaround: Use bots like DiscordChatExporter for message backups, and manually copy role/channel settings via screenshots or text files.
consequence: Without a backup, accidental deletion of a channel or role set can take hours to recreate; manual backups are rarely comprehensive and often neglected.
